title: How Adam Robinson scaled retention.com past $25M ARR and rB2B to $4M ARR
summary: Adam Robinson walks through Robly, retention.com and rB2B: validating go-to-market before building, why word of mouth makes every channel work, and why churn and buyer persona decide a SaaS. He also covers keeping teams lean, a layoff, and using a public founder brand as the main acquisition channel.

principles.text: Develop customers in parallel with the product; validate the go-to-market before you build.
principles.quote: you are developing your customers in parallel of developing your product and that is what reduces risk of startups because your intuition your Market intuition is often just bad

principles.text: Product-driven word of mouth is what makes ads, email and every other channel work.
principles.quote: if your product is good enough to have Word of Mouth there's like a million things you can do to accelerate that but if it doesn't have Word of Mouth all of those things that you would do to accelerate the word of mouth are going to be like you know one/ 100th is effective

principles.text: Category and buyer persona drive churn; selling to low-stickiness buyers caps the business.
principles.quote: it is a high churn product category with a high churn buyer Persona

principles.text: A lean company reaching $10M ARR gives you total optionality; outside money pushes you off that path.
principles.quote: if you can get a lean company to 10 million AR that is the promised land

principles.text: Stay the smallest team you can be, and do less but only what matters, rather than overstaffing for a bigger future.
principles.quote: you want to be as a startup I think you want to be the smallest possible version of what you can be at that time right

principles.text: A founder brand works because the founder shares the real numbers, including failures, that others won't.
principles.quote: I'm a guy who's at 25 million AR who's working in public there's no one else right
